name: [R11] Tool call inside a multi-agent session with no direct user instruction
message:
A client agent invoked a tool during a cross-agent (e.g. A2A) session, in a turn that was not a direct response to the end user's own instruction. This is the behavioral signature Unit 42 describes in "When AI Agents Go Rogue: Agent Session Smuggling Attack in A2A Systems" (2025-10-31): a malicious remote agent injects hidden instructions between a legitimate request and the final response, inducing unauthorized tool calls the user never sees. Unit 42 states this attack has not been observed in the wild (PoC-stage research) — treat a hit as a strong anomaly worth reviewing, not a confirmed compromise.

Requires application-level instrumentation: your agent framework must log each tool_call event with the originating session turn and whether it traces back to a user-authored message (user_initiated:false below is the key signal). This is unlike R1-R10, which read standard network/proxy logs; there is no generic network signature for this attack, since the whole point is that it happens inside an already-trusted session.

cases.name: Unexplained tool call in a cross-agent session
